resolutions.title: Task 4.4's type-level layer does not exist: the `Judgement` union has no consumer and no test
resolutions.action: Conceded and resolved by SUBTRACTION rather than by adding the missing test. The grep is right — the union had no consumer, no signature and no test. And a compile-negative could not have rescued it: `tsconfig.json` excludes `test/`, so a `@ts-expect-error` in the suite would never be typechecked by `npm run build`, and vitest transpiles without typechecking. So the type layer could not be made real with the tooling in the repo. Deleted `JudgementBase` / `ContinuationJudgement` / `ReadinessJudgement` / `Judgement`; the file comment now says there is ONE enforcement layer and records why the union was removed, so a later reader does not re-add it. Task 4.4 rewritten to claim one layer — the finding's own observation that the file's comment already contradicted the task is the tell, and claiming two layers while shipping one is precisely the defect this stage exists to make visible.

resolutions.title: "ONE computed rule, and only one" is false of what shipped — the gate_overridden agreement check is a second computed rule
resolutions.action: Correct, and it is the change-completeness discipline: the walk landed the second mechanism and left the thesis statement behind. The spec was already right (it specifies the agreement refusal and justifies it under R-crc-10); the two framing documents were not swept. `proposal.md`'s bullet now reads ONE computed rule about the record's RELATION TO ITS EVIDENCE and names the two further refusals as being about SHAPE and LOCATION — the carrier table's kind half, and the `gate_overridden` agreement constraint that retires with the field in rc04c. `design.md`'s D3 heading gained the same qualifier and a paragraph saying why neither is a counterexample, closing on what does stay off limits: whether the judgement was RIGHT, including whether the cited passes were clean, enough, or the right mode.

resolutions.title: Stage exit criterion (3) says THREE `accepted` pairs; the change ships TWO and the recommended architect note still claims the criteria are met
resolutions.action: Correct, and the omission was in the one artifact a later reader acts on. Task 6.4's architect note now opens with the exit-(3) revision as the FIRST thing to record: the number moved from THREE `accepted` pairs to TWO because task 5.1 re-derived the sort under the qualifying test this change SHIPS, and the criterion was written from the exploration's earlier sort, which counted the stale cross-reference that the shipped test disqualifies. Stated as the general form — a criterion written before the test cannot grade the test — so the architect records the reason rather than a later reader rediscovering three-versus-two and reconstructing the argument.

resolutions.title: `judgements` is the only conditional archive field with no `## Field notes` entry — and the parity instrument reads field notes
resolutions.action: Resolved with the CRITICAL above, and the instrument implication is the reason it was worth doing rather than deferring: `emit-schema-parity` derives the `## Field notes` bullet keys as well as the JSON-block keys, so an absent note is invisible to the only check that reads this file. Added the bullet — present only when a cadence judgement was taken at this seam, both admissible archive kinds named, and distinguished from `gate_overridden` (a refusal to be blocked), `user_decision` (audit outcome) and `warnings` (seam-arising notes, formed against no pass) — and added `judgements` to the opening enumeration.

resolutions.title: Pass MODE is a third observable citation edge left unsettled: a terminal readiness at archive may cite only proposal-phase passes
resolutions.action: Settled explicitly in the delta rather than left unstated, and settled the way the finding's own second option suggests: mode is DELIBERATELY NOT CHECKED. The reasoning is now written down — a proposal-phase pass genuinely CAN inform a terminal judgement (a design objection raised before apply and accepted without resolution is exactly an `accepted` pair), so refusing it would be the engine ruling on whether the cited evidence was the RIGHT evidence, which is the judgement R-crc-10 puts off limits. Edges (a) and (b) are well-formedness of the CITATION; mode would be an opinion about the JUDGEMENT. That line is what makes the third edge settled rather than overlooked.

resolutions.title: design.md's "twenty decisions, zero open questions" contradicts the engine's own explore emit and design.md's own Open Questions section
resolutions.action: Verified against the engine's own explore emit, which computes `decisions_captured: 18` and `open_questions_count: 2`. Rewritten to the stronger claim the finding proposes: eighteen decisions, two open questions both carrying standing recommendations and neither owned by this child — which shows the open questions were TRIAGED rather than absent, and no longer contradicts design.md's own Open Questions section three screens later.

resolutions.action: Fixed at the one site outside the architecture doc's ownership, exactly as the finding scopes it. `CLAUDE.md:168` now says rc04 owns replacing the override with a judgement record, names the field this change actually ships (`judgements`, whose `readiness` entry carries residuals as `accepted: [{claim, why}]` pairs), and notes that the earlier working name survives in the architecture doc as rc04's to reconcile. final_assessment: The fresh half of rc04a's system blind pair, walked in ONE SITTING with the external half and recorded on its own source. 1 CRITICAL, 6 WARNING, 4 SUGGESTION, all resolved, zero stale, none deferred. Two findings (the archive continuation record, the unenforced carrier kinds) were found independently by both halves and are certified on both records. Two resolutions went by SUBTRACTION rather than addition: the `Judgement` union was deleted once verification established that no compile-negative could ever have run against it, and the routing framing left rc04a entirely under the pair's one decision. The half's distinctive contribution is the sweep class — F6, F7, F10 and F11 are all one defect in four places, a mechanism landing while the sentence that describes it stays behind, which is the same class this program has been naming since rc02.
